# Independent audit: multiple additions, anchor credit, and exposure costs


multiple-small-shell-additions-anchor-credit-and-exposure-lp.md.
The standard-library verifier reran successfully: 17496 actual
six-base cap checks, 96 LP tests, 4200 aggregate-anchor caps,
and 20856 exposure inequalities. No correction is required.

## Aggregate credit and actual single-anchor hulls

The aggregate lower bound retains one actual cap. Either all owned
fibers are fully captured, paying E_q, or a single non-full owned
trace forces its opposite core partner to contribute at least R(u)V.
That dichotomy gives min(E_q,R(u)V), with no repeated charge of
any partner and no independent choice of endpoint tilts. The profile
inequality then pays Gamma V+E_q. Vertical caps suffice because
rho_d<Gamma_d and 2Gamma_d<1 for d>=2.

For a common anchor flipped to zero, the negative binary additions
introduce no other integer bases. A coordinate -1 forces the
representation onto negative-cube generators; extremality of every
remaining integer coordinate then forces a single negative vertex.
The displayed exposing functional is strictly maximal at each p:
losing one prescribed negative coordinate costs n+1, which dominates
any gain from all other coordinates. Thus arbitrary A_p contained
in T remain their exact fibers, and the core fibers remain T.

The finite upper covers include all additions at the chosen anchor
and isolate every other core vertex. Their signs remain strict for
the noncentroid thresholds, and vertical exposure controls each
outside candidate. This proves the exact maximum and uniqueness
without assuming independent fiber compatibility.

## Exposure LP and all-source upper bracket

The directional LP has the correct necessary threshold values:
eta_j>=1-b excludes the T at e_j, and
eta.p>=max_Ap(lambda_i)-b excludes A_p. Equality is a supporting
continuous hyperplane and has zero d-volume. Farkas has the stated
sign: a nonnegative dependence of rows must give a nonpositive
weighted right-hand side. Feasible exclusion sets give only an
upper certificate; uncertified fibers can be partly captured.

The base-only chi is the minimum of finitely many linear weight
sums over feasible strict-exposure subsets. Its homogeneity,
continuity, piecewise linearity, and E_q<=chi_q<=E follow as stated.
After flipping the anchor to zero, an owned p=-v cannot have positive
tilt along with v; therefore every owned addition must be charged.
The actual tilt 2eta excludes the certified fibers even after
raising the own canonical threshold to lambda_i(y)>=b.

The global upper bracket accounts for points outside the core.
A positive shell fiber has a vertical cap missing the entire core
and mass at most E<Gamma V. A zero-volume fiber cannot have its
base in the convex hull of the positive bases, because Minkowski
interpolation of positive full-dimensional fibers would make it
positive. A strict base separator therefore supplies a zero-mass
cap. No zero-volume candidate or source mass is discarded improperly.

## Exact six-base partial-trace obstruction

The displayed three inequalities define the bounded triangle with
vertices (-1,1),(1,-1),(1,1); its six integer points are exactly
the asserted source bases. The two added fibers are exposed, and
all generators lie in T, preserving the four core fibers.

At (0,0,g), the paired added thresholds are opposite about the
centroid of A_r. The audited paired-tail theorem pays 2Gamma a
for every normal and tilt; the own T pays Gamma V. Vertical caps
contain the own T and at least one of the two additions. The
matching canonical tilt h(z_1+z_2) has zero-volume supporting
traces on the two adjacent core fibers and excludes the opposite
core fiber. It captures exactly Gamma a from each addition.

The LP cost is exactly a: opposite outside vectors prevent both
positive required exclusions, while either alone can be excluded.
The full/empty cost also equals a. Hence the exact proper-trace
cost 2Gamma a<a is a first-order discrepancy with the binary
exposure surrogate.

For a<=rho_d V, each of the two owned-anchor centroids has the
proved lower bound Gamma V+a. The source's explicit cap cover
gives strictly smaller bounds at every other point and every
noncentroid on those two anchor fibers. The resulting exact
two-point maximizing set is valid without requiring 2a<=rho_d V:
each lower-bound group has owned mass only a.

All conclusions retain actual common tilts and full d-volume.
The LP is not promoted to an exact general depth coefficient.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
